ai.description: This 60–80 mm frog has a massive, triangular head with prominent dermal horns above the eyes. Its body is mottled brown or grey, mimicking dead leaves. It belongs to the family Megophryidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys megacephala* is best distinguished by its exceptionally large, broad head relative to its body size, which is significantly more pronounced than in other Indian *Megophrys* species.
ai.habitat: The Big-Headed Horned Frog inhabits primary evergreen forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found near mountain streams at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Big-Headed Horned Frog is a nocturnal ambush predator that remains motionless for long periods, relying on its leaf-like camouflage to surprise passing prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys megacephala* breeds in streams during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys megacephala* is endemic to the high-altitude forests of the Mishmi Hills in Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically occurring at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Big-Headed Horned Frog emits a short, metallic "cluck" or "tink" sound, typically heard from the leaf litter of its humid montane forest habitat.
